scope: Reference comparison: overview, focus, and following a source prerequisite. Recommendations only; application files unchanged.

capture.reference: Current in-app browser, screenshot bytes saved unchanged.
capture.local: Fresh isolated Chromium context, no user storage.

findings: Marble keeps names off individual points in the overview.
The current app gives large white theme and pack labels much more visual area than source points.
The current app reserves left space even without a selected concept, leaving its graph comparatively small.
Marble dims the wider graph and emphasizes selected relationships while keeping its detail card separate.
The current app also dims context and preserves coordinates, but large theme labels still compete with focused node labels.
Reference and local selected concepts differ; this comparison concerns hierarchy, not matching subject content.
The reference offers direct prerequisites, subsequent concepts, a total ancestral count and a back control.
The local app already lists direct source neighbors; optional tracing of a complete hard-edge chain would extend that behavior without rearrangement.

recommendedOrder: Make the map larger and progressively disclose labels.
Simplify theme envelopes and strengthen selected source links.
Optimize horizontal pack/node positions subject to stable themes and global hard-edge heights, with old coordinate versions preserved.
Add optional ancestor-chain tracing and theme emphasis without hiding cross-topic boundary links.
accessibilityObservations: Small visible points need enlarged hit areas plus search and keyboard-accessible neighbor lists.
Do not rely on color alone: retain text, arrows, solid/dashed distinctions.
No accessibility compliance or child comprehension test was conducted.
boundaries: Keep one global coordinate system across all views.
No age or grade routes, invented prerequisite edges, mastery inference or forced three-entry limit.
All recommendations are proposed adaptations, not claims about the mathematical meaning of Marble geometry.
